value.heading: I've tried Weight Watchers and even Ozempic — nothing has worked long term. Why would this be any different?
value.text: Weight Watchers counts points. Ozempic suppresses appetite. Neither one builds the actual habits that make results stick when you stop. This challenge is different because it works around your real life — your kids, your schedule, your kitchen. The goal isn't a number on a scale at the end of 30 days. It's that you've built a routine simple enough to keep going. That's what makes it last.

value.heading: I genuinely don't have time. I've got young kids and my days are already full — how long do the workouts actually take?
value.text: The workouts are short and done at home. We're talking 20 minutes or less. No commute, no gym, no waiting for equipment. They're designed to fit into the gaps in your day — not require you to carve out a whole new block of time you don't have.

value.heading: Is this actually free? What's the catch?
value.text: It's free. No credit card, no hidden trial. Tom runs this challenge because he wants to show you what's possible in 30 days. At the end, if you want to keep going with his full coaching programme, that option is there. But there's no obligation and no pressure. You get the full 30 days regardless.

value.heading: I've never really worked out before. Is this going to be too hard for me?
value.text: No. This challenge is built for women who are starting from scratch or coming back after a long break. The workouts are explained clearly, the nutrition guidance is practical — not complicated — and the tracking app keeps everything simple. You don't need any experience. You just need to show up.
